Seminar Title:

Intelligent Collision-Free Path Planning and Navigation of Legged Robots in Cluttered Environments using a MAVOA Technique

Seminar Type:

Progress Seminar

Department:

Mechanical Engineering

Speaker Name:

Pinaki Das ( Rollno : 523me1001)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Mechanical Seminar Hall (ME-001)

Date and Time:

24 Sep 2026 4.00 PM

Contact:

Dayal Ramakrushna Parhi

Abstract:

Path planning and navigation control of legged robots in uneven and unstructured environments
are challenging due to terrain uncertainty, stability requirements and real-time decision-making
constraints. The present report delineates intelligent, collision-free route planning and path
generation of legged robots using various integrated frameworks across complex, unknown
terrains. At first, this study introduces the key principle of the African vulture optimization
algorithm (AVOA). Subsequently, it modifies and hybridizes it with other techniques to obtain
near-optimal solutions for path efficiency and travelling schedule for the navigation of legged
robots in unknown, cluttered environments. Several aspects of the proposed optimization
technique are evaluated using MATLAB and WEBOTs simulations and validated
experimentally with a legged robot on laboratory-based unstructured terrains. Later, the results
are compared with the existing other standalone techniques using path length and navigation
time as performance metrics. Finally, experimental results indicate that the proposed technique
achieves more than 10% improvement in both path optimality and time efficiency compared to
other existing single-optimization techniques. Moreover, the deviation between simulated and
experimental results remains within 5%, confirming the robustness and practical applicability
of the proposed technique. The outputs demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed navigator
for reliably navigating legged robots in real-world environments.
